title: Cancelling the degree-zero complement in a connective universal rank-one complex
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P a bounded cochain complex of finite projective R-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] whose terms in negative degrees are zero. Assume H0 of its termwise scalar extension to every commutative R-algebra B is isomorphic to B. Then there is a bounded finite projective complex Q with zero negative terms and zero differential from degree zero to degree one, together with a homotopy equivalence P -> Q. No cancellation of a negative tail is requested.

source.place: Tags 0BCC (minimal finite free model over a local ring), 00O0 (residue-injective finite projective maps), and 00NX; degree-zero part of the fixed-affine parent normalization

proof.text: At each prime localize P. Its terms become finite free, so it is pseudo-coherent. The residue homology dimensions are finite, zero in negative degrees, one in degree zero, and zero above the support bound. Apply the local-ring minimal-free-model theorem. Its resulting model is bounded, connective, with degree-zero term the local ring A. Bounded projective representatives of one derived object are homotopy equivalent, by the Mathlib homotopy/derived comparison.

The A-algebra test identifies H0 of this model with A. With no negative term this is the kernel of A -> A^m. Its inclusion into A is multiplication by a non-zero-divisor c. Every coordinate of d(1) is killed by c, hence d=0. Thus H0 commutes with residue extension on the minimal model and, by the scalar-extended homotopy comparison, on the localization of P. Exact localization compares this with H0(P).

The identity test gives H0(P) = R up to isomorphism. Its canonical cycle inclusion j:R -> P^0 is residue-injective at every prime, by the preceding comparison. Apply the residue cokernel criterion and finite presentation/local-to-global projectivity to make coker(j) finite projective. Split j. On its complementary summand E, the differential E -> P^1 is residue-injective because the residue kernel of the full differential is exactly the R summand. Apply the same criterion to this restriction and split it too.

Cancel E and its image in degree one using the inverse of that split injection as contracting homotopy. Degree zero becomes R with zero differential; degree one becomes the finite projective cokernel; all higher terms remain unchanged. Projection and inclusion are homotopy inverses. The bounds are enlarged by zero and one if necessary. Over the zero ring all maps are zero, so P itself works.

lean.statement:
theorem connective_universalH0_zero_differential
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hf : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X n))
    (hp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective R (P.X n))
    (hconnective : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hzero : ∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] (φ : R →+* B),
      let PB := ((ModuleCat.extendScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P
      Nonempty (PB.homology 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of B B)) :
    ∃ Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (Q.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (Q.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective R (Q.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (Q.X n)) ∧
      Q.d 0 1 = 0 ∧ Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv P Q)
